en: The Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Wuben of Dongshan in Yunzhou, Collated by the Distant Descendant, the Śramaṇa Huiyin.
When the Master was young, he followed a teacher and, while reciting the *Prajñāpāramitā-hṛdaya-sūtra*, reached the passage: "It has no eyes, ears, nose, or tongue..."
The Master of the Body and Mind suddenly reached out his hand to touch his face and asked the Teacher:
"Such-and-such a person possesses eyes, ears, nose, tongue, and so forth.
For what reason does the Sūtra say they do not exist?
His teacher was startled and marveled at this, saying:
"I am not your teacher," he said,
and immediately pointed him toward Mount Wuxie to pay respects to Chan Master Lingmo. Prior to this,
the Master had traveled to various regions and first visited Nanquan.
On the anniversary of Mazu’s death, they were preparing a vegetarian feast.
Nanquan asked the assembly,
"Tomorrow we shall offer a memorial feast for Mazu."
"I do not know whether Mazu will return or not.
The assembly were all at a loss for an answer.
The Master then stepped forward and said:
"Wait until I have a companion, then I shall come.
Quan said,
"Although this boy was born later,"
"He is truly worthy of being carved and polished.
The Master said,
"Preceptor, do not despise the noble for being base."
The Master visited Mount Gui and asked, "Recently,
I heard the story of National Teacher Huizhong of Nanyang regarding 'insentient beings preaching the Dharma.'"
"I have not yet fathomed its subtlety," [the student] said.
Guishan asked,
"Does the Acharya not remember it?"
The Master said, "I remember it.
Guishan said,
"Try reciting it once for me."
The Master then raised [the case].
A monk asked:
"What is the mind of the ancient Buddha?"
The National Teacher said,
"It is the walls, the tiles, and the rubble.
The monk asked:
"Are walls, fences, tiles, and rubble not indeed insentient?
The National Teacher replied, "Yes.
The monk said:
"Do you still understand how to preach the Dharma?
The National Teacher replied,
"I constantly preach it with blazing intensity."
He spoke without ceasing.
The monk asked, "Why did I not hear it?"
The National Teacher said,
"It is because you yourself do not hear;
it cannot hinder others from hearing."
The monk said,
"I do not yet understand:
what kind of person is able to hear it?"
The National Teacher said,
"All the sages have heard it.
The monk asked, "How so?"
"Does the Master hear it?
The National Teacher said,
"I do not hear it."
The monk said,
"Since the Master has not heard it,
how do you know that the insentient can preach the Dharma?"
The National Teacher said,
"I am fortunate that I did not hear it.
Had I heard it, I would have been equal to the various sages."
"You would not hear me preaching the Dharma.
The monk said,
"In that case, sentient beings have no share [in it]."
The National Teacher said,
"I speak for the sake of sentient beings;
I do not speak for the sake of the sages."
The monk asked,
"After sentient beings hear this, what then?
The National Teacher said:
[The Master] said, "They are not sentient beings.
The monk asked,
"According to which scriptures or teachings is it said that insentient things preach the Dharma?"
The National Teacher said,
"It is evident that words which do not encompass the classics are not what a gentleman discusses."
Do you not see that the Avataṃsaka Sūtra says:
"The lands speak, sentient beings speak, and all things of the three periods of time speak"?
The Master raised the whisk.
Guishan said,
"I have it here as well."
"It is simply that such a person is rarely encountered.
The Master said,
"I have not yet attained clarity."
He requested the Master’s instruction.
Guishan held up his whisk and asked,
“Do you understand?”
The student said,
"I do not understand.
I request that the Master explain it."
Miaoyan said,
"The mouth born of one's parents will never speak for a child.
The Master said:
"Are there others who, like you, have concurrently sought the Way under the Master?
Guishan said,
"Proceed from here."
In Shixian County of Lingling, stone chambers lie connected one after another.
There is a practitioner named Yunyan;
if you can part the weeds and gaze upon the wind, you will find him.
"It must be what you value most, my son.
The teacher said,
"I do not yet understand."
"What is this person like?
Guishan said,
"He once questioned me, the old monk."
When a student wished to take leave of his teacher, how did the old monk respond? He said to him:
"You must completely sever all leaks before you may go."
He said, "Does this not accord with the Master's intent? The old monk replied,
"There is no such thing as 'not accords'."
"The First cannot attain the Way; an old monk like me resides here.
The Master then took his leave of Guishan and went directly to Yunyan.
Having recounted the preceding circumstances, he immediately asked,
"Who is it that can hear the Dharma preached by the insentient?
Yankong replied:
"Inanimate things can hear.
The Master asked,
"Does the Abbot hear?"
Yan said, "If I were to hear it,
you would not hear my preaching of the Dharma."
The Master said,
"Why do you not hear it?
Yanguan held up his whisk and said:
"Do you hear it?
The Master said, "I do not hear it.
Yankong said:
"You have not even heard me preach the Dharma;
how much less so the insentient preaching the Dharma?
The Master said:
"Which scripture or teaching does 'insentient beings preaching the Dharma' correspond to?
Yankou replied,
"Have you not seen it?"
The *Sukhāvatīvyūha Sūtra* states:
"The water birds and the forest trees all recollect the Buddha and recollect the Dharma.
At these words, the Master attained a profound realization.
He then composed a verse, saying:
"How truly marvelous, how truly marvelous!
That insentient beings preach the Dharma is inconceivable."
If one listens with the ears, it will ultimately be difficult to comprehend;
only when hearing through the faculty of the eye can one truly know.
The Master asked Yunyan:
"Such-and-such has residual habits that are not yet exhausted.
Yank said, "What have you ever done?"
The Master said,
"Even the Noble Truths are not pursued.
Yankou said:
"Are you joyful yet?
The Master said,
"It is not that I am without joy."
It is like finding a single bright pearl while scavenging through a heap of refuse.
The Master asked Yunyan:
"What is it like when you intend to meet [the Buddha]?"
He said, "I am asking the Attendant for General Affairs.
The Master said,
"While you are in the midst of asking."
Xiang said, "What did you say just now?
Yunyan raised this question and asked the Master:
"Yaoshan once asked a monk..."
When he heard it said that you understood how to calculate the real and the unreal,
you replied that you did not dare.
The Master said:
"Try to calculate this old monk for me," he said.
The monk had no reply.
"How would you do it? he asked.
The Master said:
"I request the Abbot's birthday.
On the night of Yaoshan’s formal assembly, he did not light the lamps.
Shan-ch'ui said, "I have a phrase;
I shall tell it to you once the hornless ox gives birth to a calf."
At that time, there was a monk who said,
"This is a case of a barren cow giving birth.
From then on, the Master did not speak further.
Shan said,
"Attendant, bring the lamp.
The monk withdrew from his seat and joined the assembly.
Yunyan brought this up for the Master to see.
The Master said,
"That monk, however, understands."
It was simply that he refused to prostrate.
When Yunyan arrived at Mt.
Weishan, Weishan asked him:
"Between the person who acts as a great guarantor and that [other person], which is one and which is two?
Yank said, "A single bolt of silk is one piece; it is not two pieces."
Upon hearing this, the Master said,
"It is like a person trying to uproot a tree.
One day, Yunyan said to the assembly:
There was a man’s son who could not fail to provide an answer whenever he was questioned.
The Master asked him:
"How many scriptures are there in that other house?
Yanguan replied,
"Not even a single character."
The Master said,
"How is it that you have so much knowledge?
Yank replied:
"I have not slept day or night.
The Master said,
"May I ask you about a certain matter?"
Yan said, "You have spoken the Way, yet you have not spoken it.
This was when Yunyan was making shoes.
The master stepped forward and said,
"I beg the Master for his eyes;
I do not know whether or not I shall obtain them."
Yan said, "With whom will yours go?
The Master replied:
"Good Price, I have none.
Yanguan said,
"Even if you had some, where would you put it?"
The Master remained silent. Yank asked,
"Is that which begs for eyes itself the eye?"
The Master said, "It is not the eye.
Yanyang gave a shout.
Yunyan then asked a nun:
"Is your father alive?
"He is alive," he replied. Yunyan said:
"How old are you?
He replied, "I am eighty years old. Yan said:
"You have a father;
he is not yet eighty years old—
do you know him or not?"
Yun said,
"Is it not one who comes in this manner?
Yan replied, "It is."
"Still, they are but his descendants.
The Master said,
"Even those who do not come in such a manner are likewise his descendants."
When the head monk returned from visiting the stone grotto,
Yunyan asked him,
"Did you go all the way into that stone grotto?"
"Why have you returned so soon?
The Master remained silent.
The Teacher spoke on his behalf, saying:
"Someone has already occupied it there.
Yanguan said,
"Why do you go back again?"
The Master said,
"One must not let human sentiments be severed.
The Master then took his leave of Yunyan.
Yan asked,
"Where have you gone?
The Master replied:
Although he had left his preceptor,
he had not yet determined where to stay.
[The preceptor] said, "Do not go south of Lake Hu."
The Master said, "No.
[The monk] said, "Do not return to your home village.
The Master said, "No."
[The monk] asked, "When will you return?
The Master said,
"I shall come when the Abbot has a place to stay."
[The monk] said, "From this parting, it will be difficult for us to meet again.
The Master said,
"It will be difficult not to meet again."
As the Master was about to depart, he again questioned Yunyan:
"After the Master has passed away,
should someone suddenly ask whether it is possible to capture your true likeness, what would you say?"
"How should one respond?
Yan said, "Simply say to him:"
"This alone is it.
After the Master had remained silent for a long time, Yǎn said:
"Venerable Upādhyāya, you must take up this matter with great care and scrutiny.
Later, while crossing water, he beheld his own reflection.
He attained great enlightenment regarding the original intent,
and thus composed a verse which says:
"One must by all means avoid seeking from others."
Far away, he has become distant from me;
now I go forth alone,
and everywhere I encounter him.
"He is now precisely me;
I am now not he. One must understand it in this way.
Only then did he realize suchness.
When the Master was attending Yunyan,
Yunyan asked:
"What is the merchant's supernatural power and wondrous function?
The Master stood before him with his hands joined in *añjali*.
He asked again.
"What is the wondrous function of spiritual powers?
The Master then said, "Take care," and departed.
The Master then went to visit Chan Master Baoyun of Luzu.
He prostrated and stood in attendance for a short while, then departed;
having returned once more, he entered again.
The Patriarch said, "Just so, just so;
that is why it is thus."
The Master said,
"There are many who are unwilling.
The Patriarch said:
"How can I take your verbal cleverness?
The Master then paid his respects and attended upon him for several months.
A monk asked Luzu,
"What is 'speaking without speaking'?
Luzu said:
"Where is your mouth? He replied, "I have no mouth.
The Patriarch said:
"With what will you eat your rice?
The monk had no reply.
The Master spoke on his behalf, saying:
"He is not hungry.
What kind of food does he eat?
When the Master arrived at Nan-yuan, he found Chan Master Dao-ming just as he was ascending the Dharma Hall.
Yuan said,
"I have already seen through you.
The Master then went down.
When morning came, he went back up to ask, saying,
"Yesterday I already received the Master’s compassion;
I do not know where that place was which you granted me for our mutual inspection."
Yuan said:
"Mind after mind, without interruption,
flows into the ocean of nature."
The Master said,
"How could I have let this pass?
Then the Master took his leave of Nanyuan and departed.
Yuan said,
"I have studied the Buddha-dharma extensively and performed great benefit for others.
The Master said:
[The questioner] said, "I do not ask about studying much of the Buddha-dharma;
how does one extensively bring about benefit?
Yuan said:
"Not to contradict a single thing is it.
When the Master arrived at the Pipal tree,
the Pipal asked:
"What have you come to do?
The Master said,
"To attend upon the Venerable One."
Bai said: "If it is such intimacy,
why use these two pieces of skin to move?"
The Master had no reply. Later, when Cao Shan heard of this, he said, "One son has personally attained it.
The Master then paid homage to the Venerable Xingping of Jingzhao.
Feng said,
"Do not pay homage to this old man.
The Master said:
"Rituals are not for the elderly and decrepit," Ping said.
"Furthermore, he would not accept such ritual honors."
The Master said,
"He never prostrated either.
The Master then asked:
"What is the mind of the ancient Buddhas?
He replied,
"It is simply your own mind."
The Master said, "Even so,
this is still a point of doubt for me."
Ping said,
"If that is so, then go ask the wooden man.
The Master said:
I, [Name], have a single phrase that does not borrow from the mouths of the various sages.
It is simply this:
"Try saying it yourself," [the Master] said.
The teacher replied, "It is not I."
The Master took his leave of Master Ping.
Ping asked, "Where are you going?"
The Master said:
"Flowing along the current, there is no fixed stopping place.
Ping said: "It is level."
"The Dharma-body flows along with the stream;
the Reward-body flows along with the stream.
The Master said:
Ping did not offer this interpretation at all;
he merely clapped his hands.
Baofu said:
Dongshan was a distinct lineage in his own right;
he then said separately,
"How many people have you found?"
When the Master arrived at Shushan,
Shushan said,
"You have already established yourself in one place."
"Why have you come here again?
The Master replied,
"Liang-jia can do nothing with my doubts."
"I have come specifically to see the Master.
Master Shanshan called out "Liang-jia," and the Master responded, "Yes."
Shan said, "What is this?
The Master was speechless.
Shan said,
"A fine Buddha indeed, yet he simply lacks radiance.
The Master had previously heard these words from Chief Seat Chu at Letan.
He said:
"How truly marvelous! How truly marvelous!
The realm of Buddhas and the realm of the Path are inconceivable."
The Master then asked:
"I do not ask about the Buddha-realm and the Way-realm;
I simply ask, who is it that speaks of the Buddha-realm and the Way-realm?"
At first, there was no response for a long while.
The Master said,
"Why do you not speak quickly?"
The first said,
"If one contends, one will not attain it.
The Master said:
The Way has never been spoken of.
What is there to discuss? How could it not be so?
At first, there was no response.
The Master said:
"Both 'Buddha' and 'the Way' are merely names and expressions.
Why do you not cite the teachings?"
The first asked,
"What is the teaching?
The Master said:
"When one attains the meaning, one forgets the words.
The Master said, "Even so, you are still taking the teaching and directing it toward the mind; this constitutes a sickness."
The Master said,
"How great or small is the illness of those who speak of the Buddha-realm and the Path-realm?
At first, there was no response.
The following day, he suddenly passed away.
At that time, people called the Master "The Head Seat Who Was Killed by Inquiry.
Later, the Master was traveling together with his senior teacher, Master Mi.
Seeing vegetable leaves floating in a mountain stream,
the Master said,
"The deep mountains are devoid of people."
"Why are there vegetables here?
Is there perhaps a practitioner of the Way living by this stream?
Thereupon, they deliberated together on how to part the grass.
While traveling along the mountain stream for five or seven *li*, he suddenly encountered a man of emaciated form and unusual appearance;
this was none other than National Teacher Longshan (Heshang). Also known as Yishan, the teacher set down his luggage and offered his greetings.
The mountain man said,
"This mountain has no paths.
From where have you come, O Ācārya?"
The Master said,
"Setting aside for a moment the fact that there is no path,
from where did you enter, Preceptor?"
Shan said,
"I have not come following the clouds and waters.
The Master said:
"How long has the Master resided on this mountain?
The Mountain replied,
"Not even a spring or an autumn."
The Master said,
"The Abbot has resided here first;
this mountain has resided here first."
Shan said, "I do not know.
The Master asked,
"Why do you not know?"
Shan said,
"I have not come from the realm of humans or devas.
The Master said:
"What principle have you realized, Master, that you dwell on this mountain?
The Master replied:
"I see two earthen oxen fighting their way into the sea;
even until now, there has been no news of them.
The Master then assumed his full ceremonial bearing, prostrated himself, and asked:
"What is the guest within the host?
The Master said,
"Green mountains shroud white clouds."
The Master asked,
"What is the master among masters?
Shanshan replied:
[The monk] had not gone out of his room for many years.
The Master asked,
"How far apart are host and guest?"
Shan said,
"The waves upon the waters of the Long River.
The Master said:
When the guest and host met, what was their conversation?
The Mountain said:
"The clear breeze brushes against the white moon."
The Master took his leave.
One day, while the Master was crossing a stream with his senior companion, Master Mi,
the Master said:
"Do not set foot down in error.
Baizhang said,
"If you err, you shall not pass through."
The Master said,
"What is this matter that is not mistaken?
He replied, "I am crossing the water with the Elder."
The Master and his senior teacher Mi were hoeing the tea garden.
The Master threw down his mattock and said,
"I am exhausted today."
"He has not a single bit of strength.
The elder said,
"If he has no strength, how could he possibly speak like this?"
The Master said,
"You think that one who possesses physical strength is the one [who attains it]. Once,
while the Master and his senior teacher Mi were crossing a body of water, they encountered this.
He then asked,
"What was the matter with crossing the water?
Baizhang said:
"He did not get his feet wet.
The Master said,
"An old man of my age making such talk!"
Baizhang said,
"How would you say it?
The Master replied:
His feet were not wet.
While Master Mi was holding the needle,
the Master asked him:
"What are you doing? Baizhang replied, "Holding a needle.
The Master said:
"What is the matter with the needle?
Baizhang said,
"Every stitch is identical."
The Master said,
"Having practiced together for twenty years, how could you speak such words?
Is there really no such effort?"
Baizhang said,
"What about you, Elder?
The Master replied:
Just as when a great fire breaks out upon the earth,
he asked his teacher on another day:
"There is nothing within the scope of your knowledge that you have not personally traversed."
At this direct juncture, he requested a word from the Master.
The Master said,
"How can you, my senior teacher, seek to claim credit for this?"
At this, Baizhang suddenly uttered a remark that was most extraordinary. Once,
while the Master and his senior teacher Mi were walking along,
they suddenly saw a white rabbit scurry past.
Ba said, "How eminent! Shi asked, "How so?"
Baizhang said,
"It is very much like a commoner in white robes being appointed as a high minister.
The Master said:
"You old man, you old man, making such talk!
Baizhang said,
"What about you?"
The Master said,
"For generations we have worn the official hairpins and robes, yet for a time they have fallen into obscurity.
Then the Master and his senior teacher, Master Mi, crossed a wooden bridge.
The Master first crossed over, picked up the wooden bridge, and said,
"Come over here.
Baizhang said:
"Preceptor Jia," he said,
and the Master immediately lowered the wooden bridge.
The Master was acquainted with an official.
The official said, "I,
your disciple, intend to annotate the *Sixin Ming* (Inscription on Faith in Mind) of the Third Patriarch.
The Master said:
As soon as there is right and wrong,
one becomes confused and loses one's mind.
How can this be explained?
Fayan Daoying said, "If that is so,
then I, your disciple, shall not provide a commentary.
The Master and his senior teacher Mi went together to the place of Chan Master Zhe of Boya.
Yan asked, "Where have you come from?
The Master said:
A man came from Hunan.
Yunyan asked,
"What is the surname of the Inspector General?"
The Master said,
"He has no surname.
Yankong said:
"What is its name?
The Master said,
"It cannot be named."
Yan said,
"Is there still the matter of attending to affairs?
The Master said:
"There is already a corridor and screen here.
Yan asked,
"Do you still enter and exit?"
The Master said,
"It does not enter or exit the crags. [The monk] said,
"Does it not enter and exit?"
The Master then shook out his sleeves and went out.
The next morning at dawn, Yǎn entered the hall and summoned the Master.
The Master approached him.
Yan said, "Yesterday,
when you responded to the elder's discourse, it did not satisfy this old monk's mind;
I have been ill at ease all night."
"I now request that the Elder provide a turning phrase;
if it satisfies my mind,
I shall open the gruel and stay with you to pass the summer retreat."
The Master said,
"Please ask the Abbot instead.
Yan said:
"How is it that there is no entering or exiting?
The Master said,
"It is because they are too noble."
Yan then opened the gruel and they passed the summer retreat together.
While the Master and his senior companion, Master Mi, were walking along,
he pointed to a courtyard by the roadside and said:
Inside there was someone speaking of mind and nature.
Bo asked, "Who is it?"
The Master said,
"Having been questioned by my senior teacher,
I was truly driven to the brink of death."
The Abbot said,
"Who is it that speaks of mind and speaks of nature?
The Master replied:
Having been restored to life from death,
the Master was offering incense before the portrait of Yunyan when a monk asked:
The former master said:
"It is just this. Do not simply say 'yes' or 'no'."
The Master said, "Yes.
[The monk] asked, "What is the meaning?
The Master said:
At that time, I misunderstood the former master’s meaning and asked,
"I do not yet know:
did the former master still know whether [it] exists or not?"
The Master said,
"If you did not know that [it] exists,
how could you understand such a statement?"
If one knew it existed,
how could one willingly speak in such a way?
Changqing said:
Since you already know that it exists,
why do you speak in this way?
It is further said:
Only after raising a child does one come to know a father’s compassion.
On the anniversary of Yunyan’s death, the Master prepared a vegetarian feast.
A monk asked:
"What instructions did the Master receive from Yunyan?
The Master replied,
"Although I was there..."
"I did not receive any instruction.
[The Master] said, "Since you did not receive any instruction,
what is the use of holding a vegetarian feast?"
The Master said,
"How would I dare go against him?
[The monk] said, "But the Master's own departure was from Nanquan."
"Why then did you offer a vegetarian feast for Yunyan?
The Master said,
"It was not that I held my late teacher's moral virtue or Buddhist Dharma in high regard."
He simply valued him so much that he did not explain it through for me.
The monk said,
"The Master is holding a vegetarian feast for his late teacher."
"Would you agree with the former master or not?
The Master replied,
"Half agreed, half not agreed."
[The student] asked, "Why do you not fully approve?
The Master said,
"If I were to fully approve, I would be failing my former teacher."
Question: "I wish to see the Original Teacher of my *upādhyāya*.
How may I see him? The Master said:
"When age and teeth correspond, there will be no obstruction.
As the monk was about to offer a word in response,
the Master said:
Without following the previous track,
he asked another question separately.
The monk had no reply.
Yunju spoke on behalf [of the monk], saying:
"In that case, you do not see the Master's original teacher.
A monk asked Changqing:
"What is it that is like the teeth of a year?
Qingyun said,
"The ancients spoke thus."
"Upādhyāya, what more do you seek here? At that time,
an official had prepared a vegetarian feast and offered pure wealth,
inviting the Master to oversee the recitation of the Tripitaka.
The Master descended from his meditation seat and bowed toward the official;
the official bowed to the Master.
The Master then led the official to circumambulate the meditation seat once.
He bowed toward the official and,
after a long pause, asked:
"Do you understand?"
He said, "I do not understand.
The Master said,
"I shall show you how to turn the Great Tripitaka."
"How could it not be so? He ascended the hall and said:
"Is there anyone who does not requite the four debts of gratitude and the three realms of existence?"
The assembly was speechless.
He spoke again, saying:
"If you do not embody this meaning..."
Regarding the affliction of beginning and end:
one must simply ensure that mind after mind does not touch external objects,
and step after step remains without a fixed location.
Only by maintaining constant, uninterrupted practice can one attain correspondence with the truth.
You must exert yourself directly;
do not let the days pass in idleness.
A monk asked,
"When cold and heat arrive, how can one avoid them?
The Master said:
"Why do you not go to a place where there is neither cold nor heat?
He asked, "What is this place where there is neither cold nor heat?
The Master said:
"When it is cold, it kills you, O *śrāmaṇera*;
when it is hot, it kills you, O *śrāmaṇera*.
He then ascended the hall and said:
When the teachings of the patriarchs and Buddhas seem like an enemy, only then does one have the capacity for study;
if you cannot penetrate these teachings,
you will be deceived by them.
Ascending the hall, he said:
"Severing the way of the host,
one does not fall into a secondary view."
Beiyuan stepped forward from the assembly and said,
"One must know that there is one person who does not join the company.
The Master said:
This was still his second view.
The Master then overturned the meditation seat.
The teacher said:
"Old brother, what do you say?
The Master said,
"I will tell you, Teacher, once my tongue has rotted away."
At the morning assembly,
Shushan Ren came forward and asked,
"I request the Master to provide instruction regarding the words that have not yet arisen."
The Master said,
"If one does not agree, no one will be willing.
Shu said, "..."
"Can you still cut it?
The Master said,
"Can you cut it right now?"
Shu said: "By all means, do not immediately take that which is beyond naming as the point of no-avoidance.
